name: Apply a camera input transform before the film stock
covers: trilinear LUT application before creative stock rendering
description: Verifies a camera input LUT is loaded, validated and applied before the selected film emulation.
steps: Open Video Lab and import a supported clip
Select a film stock and compare the preview
Try an invalid or incomplete .cube file
expected: A valid LUT is applied before the film stock, its name and grid size are shown, and invalid LUT files produce a visible error.

name: Browse film families and render a graded video
description: Verifies the expanded shared stock library works in the video workspace.
steps: Select the stock and play a supported clip
expected: The selected stock grades the preview and a WebM file is produced.

name: Use Rec.709 footage without an input LUT
description: Verifies standard display-referred footage can be graded without an additional camera input transform.
steps: Leave the input LUT empty and choose a stock
expected: The Rec.709 clip can be processed without loading a camera LUT and the stock controls remain usable.

name: Film stocks have distinct rendering signatures
description: Checks that representative negative, slide, cinema, monochrome and instant stocks use distinct response signatures rather than a shared generic filter.
steps: Open Video Lab and import a Rec.709 clip with skin, foliage, sky and bright highlights
Compare Kodak Portra 400, Gold 200 and Ektar 100
Compare Ilford HP5, Kodak T-Max 400 and Tri-X
Pause on a frame and verify the grain is stable; play and verify grain evolves over time
expected: Each selected stock produces a visibly distinct palette and tonal response. Black-and-white stocks use different spectral mixes and grain character. The same paused frame remains deterministic while moving frames receive evolving grain.
